chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is recommended that you say between the Corner and the Stone: 'O Allah, grant us good in the world and good in the Hereafter, and save us from the punishment of the Fire.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'An appointed angel says: Ameen.'

key_terms.الرُّكْن: The Corner (specifically the Yemeni Corner of the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite between the Rukn and Hajar during Tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi prescribes a specific supplication between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone, echoing the Quranic plea for dual goodness while adding a petition for deliverance from the Fire. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual efficacy of this location, noting that an angel recites 'Ameen' to affirm the supplicant's request. This practice underscores the interconnection between ritual movement (Tawaf) and intimate divine dialogue within Shia devotional life.
